subject: Clearstream dedicated performance pilot — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearstream.ai>, Ashwin Rao <ashwin@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clearstream dedicated performance pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Priya / Ashwin —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery + what we heard you need from a Dedicated capacity pilot: 

Summary of SLOs you asked us to validate
- Streaming / incremental response requirement: partial token flushes to client as model generates (low-latency streaming).
- Latency target: p95 <= 120 ms for short responses (single-turn); for streaming sessions we’re targeting p95 partial-chunk latency <= 140 ms depending on chunk-size.
- Throughput: baseline sustained traffic equivalent to ~300 tokens/sec across active streams, peak bursts up to 1,200 tokens/sec for short windows.
- Concurrency: ~50–70 concurrent streaming sessions during peak.

Key constraints you flagged
- Customer-visible tail latency is critical (any p99 spikes > 500 ms are a problem).
- Workload mix: ~60% short completions (<=40 tokens), ~40% multi-chunk streaming sessions (200–600 tokens total).
- Model family: you expect to run a 7B-class model for production pilot; may test a 13B variant for a subset of routes.

Next steps we propose
1) You share a 24–72 hour sample traffic trace (anonymized) — we’ll use it to synthesize a replay for our test harness.
2) Redwood runs a two-week Dedicated pilot: reserved pool + autoscale for burst windows. We recommend an initial reserved pool config (technical details to follow from our SE).
3) If pilot validates SLOs, we can convert to a month commitment and scope production rollout.

Attachments: throughput matrix (clearstream_throughput_matrix_v1.csv), initial cost sketch (pilot_config_estimate.xlsx).

Questions for you to confirm:
- Is the p95 <= 120 ms requirement for short completions still the correct bar?
- Are there any extra compliance/region constraints we should bake into the pilot (e.g., VPC-only)?
- Timeline: can you sign off to start a pilot the week of Aug 9?

Thanks — will loop in Aditya (SE) and Tessa (Solutions) on the technical plan.

—
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearstream.ai>

Cc: Ashwin Rao <ashwin@clearstream.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clearstream dedicated performance pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Naomi — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side so the pilot can be scoped correctly:

- Latency: we confirm p95 <= 120 ms for short completions (<=40 tokens). For streaming sessions we are flexible up to p95 <= 160 ms for individual chunk flushes as long as overall session latency (time-to-first-chunk) stays low.
- Throughput / concurrency: the 300 tokens/sec baseline is roughly what our current prod sees, but to be safe we want capacity for sustained 500 tokens/sec and the ability to handle 1,500 tokens/sec bursts for up to 2 minutes. Concurrent sessions target: 60 active streaming sessions.
- Models: start with your recommended 7B inference profile; we will run a 13B smoke test during the pilot but the primary SLOs are against the 7B.
- Compliance: VPC peering only for pilot; no public ingress.

A few asks: can you provide a short comparative note on GPU sizing (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and an expected reserved throughput number we should expect on the invoice? Also share the data anonymization checklist for the traffic trace we’ll send.

If we can get those items today we’ll aim to sign the pilot SOW and get PO to procurement@clearstream.ai by Fri Aug 6.

Regards,
Priya
Head of Platform Engineering | Clearstream Analytics
priya.shah@clearstream.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearstream.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clearstream dedicated performance pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Priya — quick technical breakdown and recommended pilot config below. My comments assume the 7B model architecture you mentioned and streaming chunk sizes ~32–64 tokens per flush.

GPU tradeoffs (summary)
- H100 (best latency / concurrency): strong for low p95 streaming at high concurrency. Recommended when tail latency and per-token latency matter most. For 7B streaming with 60 concurrent sessions, we expect p95 partial-chunk latency ~80–110 ms (single-region placement, NVLink disabled).
- A100 (balanced): good throughput for batched workloads and dense batching windows. For continuous streaming at high concurrency, p95 commonly sits in the 110–150 ms range under similar load.
- L4 (cost-optimized): best for cost-sensitive workloads with low concurrency; p95 can be 160–280 ms depending on quantization and KV cache hit-rate. Not recommended as sole pilot hardware for your latency targets.

Reserved throughput guidance
- Based on your stated baseline and headroom ask, we recommend reserving 5,000 tokens/sec for the pilot pool (this gives ~10x headroom over baseline 500 tokens/sec and accommodates burst coalescing).
- If you want a lower-commitment option, a 2,000 tokens/sec reserved pool with autoscale-to-4 nodes for bursts is possible but increases the risk of transient p95 spikes during sustained bursts.

Suggested pilot config (two-week run)
- Reserved pool: 2 x H100 (dedicated), pin model v1.0 (7B), reserved throughput 5,000 tokens/sec, autoscale cap to 4 x H100 for burst windows.
- Networking: VPC peering + private control plane (no public ingress).
- Observability: enable token-level tracing, per-route dashboards, and a short evaluation prompt-set to gate quality regressions.
- Validation plan: Redwood will run a replay of your anonymized 72-hour trace and an additional synthetic burst test (1.5k tokens/sec for 2-minute windows) and produce a runbook with p95/p99 numbers and cost estimate.

Numbers (approx)
- H100 (2-node reserved): expected sustained p95 ~90–110 ms for 7B streaming at 60 concurrent sessions; estimated cost shown in attached PDF (redwood_gpu_tradeoffs_summary.pdf).
- A100 (2-node reserved): expected sustained p95 ~120–150 ms; better batch throughput but higher tail for streaming.

Next steps we can action immediately
1) Naomi / Vivek to provision a pilot SOW draft and SOW link (HubSpot).
2) Priya to share anonymized trace + confirmation on reserved throughput (5,000 tokens/sec preferred) and PO timeline.
3) Redwood will schedule a kickoff runbook and assign an SE for the replay (Tessa).

Relevant links: pilot runbook preview: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AExampleRunbook (internal read-only), HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CLST-2027-042.

—
Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We are happy to proceed with the 2 x H100 reserved pool + autoscale to 4 for a two-week pilot, reserved throughput 5,000 tokens/sec, VPC peering only.

Procurement will issue the PO to procurement@clearstream.ai by EOD Fri Aug 6. Please send the SOW and pilot kickoff invite; include Tessa for the replay/validation windows.
